[...] ''I don't see anything except the end of the fight. I don't even see a living being. I don't have any connection to the opponent at all. I just see something I have to remove, stop, get past, any way I can, to get what I want—or die.''"<br />"''Wow.''"<br />"''Some fancy doctor said we can switch on ''psychopathy''.|[[Jedi Knight/Legends|Jedi Knight]] [[Jaina Solo Fel|Jaina Solo]] and [[Mandalorian/Legends|Mandalorian]] [[Soldier/Legends|soldier]] [[Goran Beviin]]|<ref name="Revelation">''[[Legacy of the Force: Revelation]]''</ref>}}
'''Psychopathy''', or '''sociopathy''', was a personality disorder where a being had a lack of emotion or remorse, egocentricity, anti-social and abusive behavior, and were able to pass themselves off as normal by feigning emotion or lying about their past.

During the [[Mandalorian Wars]], the former [[Jedi/Legends|Jedi]] [[Padawan/Legends|Padawan]] [[Zayne Carrick]] deduced that [[Chantique]], the [[Magister Impressor]] of [[The Crucible]], was a psychopath and that [[Demagol]], the [[Mandalorian/Legends|Mandalorian]] mad scientist, was a sociopath.<ref name="KotOR 48">[[Knights of the Old Republic 48|''Knights of the Old Republic'' 48]]</ref>

[[Redline]] was described by [[Captain/Legends|Captain]] [[Juno Eclipse/Legends|Juno Eclipse]] as a psychopath during her time flying with him.<ref name="The Force Unleashed novel">[[Star Wars: The Force Unleashed (novelization)|''Star Wars: The Force Unleashed'' novelization]]</ref> [[Blaschowwa]] was a [[Wookiee/Legends|Wookiee]] [[Pirate/Legends|pirate]] altered by [[Dark Jedi/Legends|Dark Jedi]] [[Thaum Rystra]] with [[Sith alchemy/Legends|Sith alchemy]] and one of the side effects made him a psychopath.<ref name="[[Light and Dark (adventure)|Light and Dark]]">"[[Light and Dark (adventure)|Light and Dark]]"</ref> Many considered [[Bounty hunter/Legends|bounty hunter]] [[Aurra Sing/Legends|Aurra Sing]] to be a psychopath.<ref name="Star Wars Adventures 6: The Warlords of Balmorra">''[[Star Wars Adventures 6: The Warlords of Balmorra]]''</ref> Count Dooku's disregard for life, even when he was a Jedi, was such that he was a borderline sociopath.

One of the most notable examples of a psychopath was [[Palpatine/Legends|Palpatine]] who, in reality, was the [[Sith Lord/Legends|Sith Lord]] Darth Sidious. He displayed superficial charm, hiding behind the guise of a kind, mild-mannered [[Senator/Legends|Senator]] from [[Naboo/Legends|Naboo]] and maintaining this demeanor as [[Supreme Chancellor/Legends|Supreme Chancellor of the Galactic Republic]]. After his ascent to the position of [[Emperor/Legends|Emperor]], Palpatine dropped the charade and everyone saw him for what he was. His psychopathy was also prevalent even prior to becoming a Sith lord, evidenced by his delinquent behavior at an adolescent age, and later his committing manslaughter on two pedestrians via a speeder.<ref name="DPN">[[Darth Plagueis (novel)|''Darth Plagueis'']]</ref> [[40 ABY/Legends|Years after]] his [[Death/Legends|death]], during her [[Duel at The Home|duel with Jacen Solo]], Lumiya alluded to Palpatine, saying he was a "psychopath consumed by power."<ref name="[[Legacy of the Force: Betrayal]]">''[[Legacy of the Force: Betrayal]]''</ref>. Palpatine's manipulative behavior cannot be exaggerated as he manipulated the entire galaxy into doing his bidding. He was likened to a Dejarik master, moving people the way one would move pieces on a board. So great was Palpatine's façade of benevolence and normalcy that he was almost able to feign tears whilst persuading Senator Amidala to accept Jedi protection, saying "the thought of losing you is unbearable." He was intensely sadistic, taking great pleasure from killing Mace Windu and torturing Luke Skywalker with his lightening powers. Palpatine was prone to asserting himself in a grandiose and narcissistic manner, claiming that he was "the greatest Sith Lord the galaxy had ever known" and also identifying his soul with the blackness of space, reassuring himself "I am the universe."

[[Incinerator stormtrooper/Legends|Incinerator stormtroopers]], in order to increase their effectiveness in razing targets, were also bred to have a psychopathic urge to destroy things. The [[Director of Imperial Intelligence]] [[Ysanne Isard]] was described by Captain [[Sair Yonka]] as sociopathic when informing her of his reason for defecting from her faction of the Galactic Empire.

[[Goran Beviin]], a [[Mandalorian/Legends|Mandalorian]] [[Soldier/Legends|soldier]], explained to [[Jaina Solo Fel|Jaina Solo]] in [[41 ABY]] that Mandalorians had been diagnosed with the ability to "switch on" psychopathy by a [[Psychologist/Legends|psychologist]]. He stated that it was a mindset his people were trained to master when they were young, explaining that the trait was what had provoked him to lose control and ferociously attack Solo during a [[Lightsaber duel/Legends|training duel]] on [[Mandalore/Legends|Mandalore]]. The commonly even-tempered Beviin found the ability to turn on psychopathy somewhat concerning—remarking to a troubled Solo that it had a frightening effect upon even him—but recognized its usefulness in battle, even recommending that Solo consider adapting the skill. However, Solo found the Mandalorian's induced psychopathy technique brought a [[Jedi/Legends|Jedi]] too close to the [[Dark side of the Force/Legends|dark side of the Force]], and rejected it.<ref name="Revelation" />

==Behind the scenes==
The terms psychopathy and sociopathy refer to the real-world diagnosis of [[Wikipedia:Antisocial personality disorder|antisocial personality disorder]]. The features of this condition include a pervasive pattern of disregard for, and violation of, the rights of others. Such individuals, while displaying witty and charming traits, would fail to conform to social norms, would be deceitful, and demonstrate a lack of remorse.<ref name="DSM-IV">{{BookCite|title=Diagnostic and Statistical Manual of Mental Disorders|pages=645 to 650}}</ref><ref name="Antisocial">{{WebCite|url=https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/pubmedhealth/PMHT0024893|text=Antisocial personality disorder|work=PubMed Health|archivedate=20150511190244}}</ref>
